quotes.text: The main identity record stays in Entra ID. Users and groups from Entra ID copy into the managed domain so the older app can see and use them in the form it understands.
quotes.why: Explains the one-way identity flow that defines how the managed domain is administered.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: For cloud-only users, that often means the user needs to change their password after domain services is enabled. That password change creates the protected form needed for the managed domain.
quotes.why: Names the most common setup pitfall and its fix in plain terms.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: But don't pick domain services just because you're using Azure. A new cloud app should sign in directly through Entra ID.
quotes.why: Clear recommendation on when not to use the service.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Choosing a managed domain means accepting a trade-off. Microsoft takes care of the domain controllers and you give up some of the control that comes with running them yourself.
quotes.why: Sums up the core managed-service trade-off in one sentence.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Keep the managed domain private inside Azure networking. It should support only the workloads that need it, not become a general company directory.
quotes.why: Concrete security guidance for operating the managed domain.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: The cloud app that still expects a Windows domain
Why Entra ID alone cannot run every legacy app
What Microsoft Entra Domain Services actually is
Entra ID, Active Directory and Domain Services: different jobs
When Domain Services fits and when it does not

takeaways: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides a managed Windows domain inside an Azure virtual network for legacy apps that still need LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, domain join or Group Policy, without you running domain controllers.

Identity data flows one way, from on-premises Active Directory or Entra ID into the managed domain, so users and groups must be managed in the source directory, and cloud-only users may need a password change before they can use it.
New cloud apps should sign in directly through Entra ID; Domain Services does not fit apps that need LDAP write access, schema changes or full domain admin control.
hook: Moving an old Windows app to an Azure VM does not remove its need for a classic domain with LDAP, Kerberos and Group Policy. This Knowledge Nugget shows IT admins and cloud architects where Microsoft Entra Domain Services fits next to Entra ID and Active Directory, and which limits to check before choosing it.
